git.head_commit_subject: docs: record installed recall acceptance and correct snapshot target history
git.note: All 15 source files referenced below were clean (no working-tree diff vs HEAD) at capture time; git status --porcelain confirmed zero of them appear in the modified/untracked list.

purpose: Retrieval-evidence cohort for evaluating code-navigation (file+symbol location), not end-to-end coding quality. Ground truth was derived by direct source inspection (Read/Grep on the working tree at the recorded HEAD), never by running any recall/retrieval tool against these questions.

schema.task_type: 'natural_language' (query contains no symbol/function/class name) or 'exact_symbol' (query is the bare symbol name — the 5 flagged tasks)
schema.is_exact_symbol_task: boolean flag duplicating task_type for easy filtering; true for exactly 5 tasks
schema.query: the natural-language question a navigator would be given, OR for exact_symbol tasks, an instruction naming the literal symbol to locate
schema.expected_path: repo-relative path of the file containing the definition, verified via `git show HEAD:<path>`
schema.expected_symbol: Python-qualified name (Class.method or bare function name) exactly as defined in source
schema.symbol_lookup: plain bare identifier string (no qualification) suitable for a literal grep/symbol-search — the minimal string that should locate the definition
schema.evidence: source line number(s) and a verbatim snippet copied from the file at the recorded git blob, proving the symbol exists exactly where claimed
schema.source_hash: git blob SHA-1 (git ls-tree/hash-object identity) and a SHA-256 of the file's raw bytes at HEAD, both independent of this cohort's own tooling
